overview: The Nara period saw Japan's first permanent capital established at Heijo-kyo, modeled on the Chinese Tang capital Chang'an. Buddhism received state patronage, the ritsuryo legal system was established and major literary works compiled.

items.text: The Manyoshu compiled, containing over 4,500 poems.
The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki chronicles record Japanese mythology and early history.
Todaiji Temple and its Great Buddha statue constructed.
Buddhism becomes a state religion with temples in every province.
The ritsuryo legal code adapted from Tang Chinese models.
Confucian ethics emphasized in government and education.
Chinese writing system fully adopted for government administration.
Road system and postal stations established.
Nara's Buddhist temples remain UNESCO World Heritage sites.
The Manyoshu remains a foundational work of Japanese literature.

fall.text: The capital moved to Heian-kyo in 794, beginning the Heian period.
